In a big move that will benefit lakhs of provident fund subscribers, the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ). The Times of India had first reported about the proposal being under consideration today. Under the proposed facility, members will be able to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in instalments over a period of time instead of taking out the entire amount at once. What is EPFO’s SWP for your PF account?
 The SWP is intended to help members turn their retirement savings into a regular and predictable source of income while retaining ownership of the underlying corpus, according to an ANI report quoting EPFO. At present, members are required to withdraw their entire provident fund corpus within three years of retirement to avoid their accounts becoming inoperative and ceasing to earn annual interest. If a member dies while receiving payments, the nominee or dependent will have the option of withdrawing the remaining balance or continuing to receive periodic payouts. Join conversation

 According to the EPFO, the initiative will strengthen financial security after retirement by offering a flexible and dependable income stream while protecting the interests of members’ families. The plan would give crores of existing subscribers access to the facility as well, particularly those who find it difficult to manage their retirement savings prudently. The proposal was discussed at a meeting of the central board of trustees on Thursday, chaired by Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya. According to the TOI report, in its initial phase, the voluntary scheme is expected to focus on existing EPFO subscribers. The organisation estimates that around 6.3 lakh members aged above 55 years could benefit from the facility at the outset.
